name: Muse Three.js 4: evaluation, export and the improvement loop
description: Adds the measurement side: an eval harness with pass@k, a model comparison report with a screenshot grid, hardened GGUF export and Ollama helpers, a rejection-sampling round that feeds passing student scenes back into training, and a docs consistency test. Numbers in the docs stay 'not measured' until the owner runs the models.

userStories.title: eval_model.py: one command per model
userStories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want a single command that evaluates any model on the held-out briefs so that every model is measured the same way.
steps: Create scripts/eval_model.py `--name NAME --briefs data/briefs.eval.jsonl [--k 1] [--ollama-native|--base-url URL] --model M`: for each brief generate k samples (ids `<id>__s1` to `__sk`, temperature 0.7 for k>1), via teacher_generate's call path, into eval/<name>/raw; then run the validator into eval/<name>/validation.jsonl and shots into eval/<name>/shots.

Write eval/<name>/summary.json: first-attempt pass rate (sample 1 only), pass@k when k>1 (a brief passes if any sample passes), pass rate by level, reason counts, median output tokens, median seconds per scene and tokens per second (from usage; 'not measured' when absent), and the model and settings used.
Resumable: existing raw files are skipped; `--skip-generate` only revalidates.
Tests with a fake generator and a fake validator runner: pass@k arithmetic, first-attempt rate ignores later samples, by-level grouping, resume skips existing raw files.
acceptanceCriteria: For fixtures where sample 2 passes and sample 1 fails, first-attempt is 0 and pass@2 is 1 for that brief (asserted)
summary.json records the model name, base URL or Ollama flag, k, temperature and the brief file used
`--skip-generate` makes zero model calls (asserted)
docs/05-export-serve-eval.md shows the three baseline commands
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

userStories.title: compare_evals.py: report and screenshot grid
userStories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want the models compared in one table and one visual grid so that the result is clear at a glance and quotable.
steps: Create scripts/compare_evals.py: reads eval/*/summary.json and writes eval/eval-report.md (a table: model, first-attempt pass rate, pass@k, median seconds per scene, tokens per second, top failure reason) plus the pass rate by level for each model.
Write eval/compare.html: one row per eval brief, one column per model, each cell the sample-1 screenshot (relative path) with a green or red border; missing screenshots show the failure reason text.
Never print a number that is not in a summary file; models without a field show 'not measured'.
Tests on fixture summaries: table content, missing field handling, HTML has a cell for every brief and model.
acceptanceCriteria: A model with no timing data shows 'not measured' in the table (asserted)
compare.html has exactly briefs x models cells for the fixture (asserted)
README.md lists compare_evals.py as the last pipeline step
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

userStories.title: Export and Ollama helpers, hardened
userStories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want export failures to be clear and checkable before I spend an hour converting so that a wrong path or missing tool is caught in seconds.
steps: Harden scripts/export_gguf.sh: verify LLAMA_CPP_DIR, convert_hf_to_gguf.py and llama-quantize exist before any work; add `--dry-run` printing the plan; fail with a one-line message naming the missing item.

Create scripts/ollama_create.sh `<gguf-dir> <name>`: builds the Modelfile (system prompt from prompts/system.txt with any triple quote escaped, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.95, top_k 30, repeat_penalty 1.0, num_ctx 16384), runs `ollama create`, supports `--dry-run`.
Move Modelfile generation into one place used by both scripts so settings cannot drift.

Tests (subprocess, fake PATH): missing llama.cpp reports the right missing file, dry-run prints every step and runs nothing, the Modelfile contains the system prompt exactly once and the five parameters.
acceptanceCriteria: export_gguf.sh --dry-run with a missing LLAMA_CPP_DIR exits non-zero naming the directory (asserted)
The generated Modelfile contains the pinned sampling parameters and the unmodified system prompt (asserted)
docs/05-export-serve-eval.md notes the llama.cpp Qwen3.5 support is unverified until the owner runs it
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

userStories.title: rejection_sampling.py: the improvement round
userStories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want passing scenes from the trained student added to the training data so that a second training round learns from verified outputs.
steps: Create scripts/rejection_sample.py `--briefs data/briefs.jsonl --name NAME --k 4 --model M [--ollama-native|--base-url URL]`: samples k scenes per training brief (never eval briefs) via the eval path, validates, and keeps passing samples that are not near-duplicates of existing training rows or each other (reuse build_dataset's dedupe).
Write kept rows in the same prompt/completion format with `source: rs` to data/rs/train.jsonl, and a run summary with kept, dropped and per-level counts.
Add `--extra data/rs` to build_dataset.py to append those rows to the training split (never to the validation split).
Tests with fakes: eval briefs excluded, duplicates dropped, rs rows only reach train, source tag present.
acceptanceCriteria: A brief whose id appears in briefs.eval.jsonl is never sampled (asserted)
rs rows appear in train.jsonl and never in val.jsonl (asserted)
docs/04-training.md describes the second round and says it is optional and unmeasured
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

steps: Write tests/py/test_docs.py: every `scripts/...` or `docs/...` path mentioned in README.md and docs/*.md exists; every file in scripts/ with a main (py, mjs, sh) is mentioned in README.md; relative links in docs resolve.

Create docs/10-results.md: a table template for the three baselines with every metric cell 'not measured', the exact commands that produce each number, and a rule that numbers are copied only from eval/eval-report.md.
Update README.md: the final pipeline table covering every stage and script, the Ralph section pointing to ralph/README.md, and the order of the docs.
Fix any broken reference the new test finds in the existing docs.

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Evaluating real models, converting GGUF and sampling from a trained student are manual gates; Ralph builds and tests the tools with mocks and fixtures.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use fixtures under tests/fixtures and mocked HTTP. Never call Baseten, Meta, Hugging Face or any remote service from a story, a test or a script you run. The only network use allowed is `npm install` and `.venv/bin/pip install` of packages the story names.
Never commit, push, tag or publish. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Never delete, overwrite or reformat anything under data/, out/, eval/, .env or .venv. They are the owner's data (a long Glimmer generation run may be writing data/raw right now). Tests write only to temporary directories.

Do not start long jobs. Any command that would run more than about 5 minutes (corpus generation, training, GGUF conversion, evals) is written as a script plus docs and left for the owner. A live smoke call to the local Ollama is allowed only if the story says so, with at most 2 briefs, and must skip cleanly when Ollama is down. Never rent GPUs or run `runpodctl` with anything that creates a pod.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests and the doc the story names. Do not change prompts/system.txt: every existing raw answer was generated against it.

Match the surrounding code: short comments that explain why, argparse CLIs, resumable file-per-item outputs, no new dependency the story does not name. Python runs with `.venv/bin/python`; Node scripts are ESM `.mjs` (Node 22).
Three.js stays pinned at 0.160.0 and the validator keeps serving the local copy in place of the CDN URL.
Python scripts must stay importable without heavy deps: import torch, transformers, trl or peft only inside functions or under `if __name__ == '__main__'` so pytest can import them.
Record only real results. Never invent pass rates, token counts, timings or costs; where a number is unknown write 'not measured'.
Debug output goes to data/ or a temp dir, never into scripts/ or docs/.
If the spec is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in `notes`. If you cannot finish a story, set `notes` to why and stop; do not mark it passing.

The completion tag is matched literally by the harness. Write it only when every acceptance criterion holds. When a criterion cannot hold yet, never type the tag, not even inside a sentence saying you are not using it; write 'no completion signal this iteration' instead.

universal: `bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names
chromium: Browser-driven tests run against the installed Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` is already done); if Chromium cannot launch, say so in `notes` instead of skipping silently

manualGates: Owner evaluates the baselines (untouched Qwen3.5-4B, local Glimmer, the trained student) on data/briefs.eval.jsonl and fills docs/10-results.md from eval/eval-report.md
Owner runs scripts/export_gguf.sh on the trained model and checks llama.cpp recognises the Qwen3.5 architecture
